criterion: Keep an image only if it shows the labelled item or material as a scrap collector would actually encounter it, as a main subject of the photo. Correct-but-difficult images (odd angle, clutter, poor light) are KEPT. Removed: a different object; documents, ledgers, adverts, posters, charts and drawings; museum or archaeological artefacts (these also carry measurement scale bars the model can learn as a shortcut); landscapes and people-focused photos where the item is incidental; and images duplicated into another class.

newspaper.note: Only 11 real newspapers. Removed: 10 library archive shelves from 'newspaper stack' searches (16-25), movie posters, soldiers, a tank, drawings, a van, a lighthouse, a stamp sheet.

books.note: Mostly genuine. Removed: Capitol-building crowd, a 'Books Rule' sign, an alarm clock, a window drawing, a sculpture, a card catalogue, a garden sculpture. Many kept images are library shelves: correct label, but unlike scrap book bundles (domain gap).

cardboard.note: Mostly genuine boxes. Removed: jungle landscape, bento lunch box, shop interior, unclear compartment tray, metal tin, trailer.

magazine.note: 11 kept after 3 query rounds: magazine racks/displays and dense cover walls where magazines are the main subject. Removed: kiosk exteriors/street scenes, ruins, parks, people, cover-art scans. WEAK CLASS - display shots, not scrap-style stacks; recommend real photos.

hard_plastic.note: Only 10 genuine. Search matched the 'Crate' guitar-amplifier brand (2,3,6), the Crate & Barrel store (0,26) and ~20 wooden crates or chests. Nearly every kept image is a plastic crate; buckets, chairs and broken plastic items are absent.

soft_plastic_film.note: Removed silage hay bales, people, a solid red frame, machinery, medical containers, street bins with no film visible, a seagull, landscapes, a school building.

iron_scrap.note: 18 kept: scrap piles, cranes with magnets, scrapyards. Removed: 22 ledger pages (12-33), chemical bottle, people photos, ornate gates, vehicle junk (belongs to car class), poster, landscapes where scrap is incidental.

stainless_steel.note: 40 kept: stainless utensils, cutlery, kitchen tools - the main stainless scrap a kabadiwala sees. Removed: P-51 planes (stainless keyword trap), food/buffet shots, vintage adverts, art sculpture, rusty (non-stainless) steel.

copper_scrap.note: 16 kept after re-query: bare copper wire, magnet wire, cable cross-sections, tube coil, plumbing fittings, busbars, copper vessels. Removed: archaeology with scale bars, B&W archives, brass-colored items (brass-class confusion), diagrams, ambiguous/dark wires.

aluminium_scrap.note: Mostly crushed-can bales. Removed: a bar chart, one locomotive photographed three times, can-craft ornaments, a pen, a globe statue, parade and fair photos, a nutrition label, a snack bag.

brass_scrap.note: Removed 10 ancient Roman coins and archaeological fragments (scale-bar shortcut), 6 rotated copies of one wooden clock figurine, foundry photos, archive document scans, a ruler photo, a duplicated sculpture. Kept: genuine Indian brass utensils, highly relevant.

ac.note: Excellent: 39 genuine, mostly rusty window units in real scrap condition. Largely one uploader's numbered series, so near-duplicates are grouped to prevent train/test leakage.

refrigerator.note: 13 of the kept images (16-28) are one home-improvement-store shoot, grouped. Removed: a railway refrigerator car, a motorcyclist, adverts, a logo badge, a display icon, food close-ups, an antique-shop interior.

washing_machine.note: Removed 9 installation photos of power sockets, pipes and taps (18-26), drum and door-seal close-ups, control-panel close-ups, shop fronts and street scenes, and antique wooden tub washers (museum artefacts).

microwave_oven.note: Removed 7 countertop trim-kit installation photos (22-28) and 8 near-identical close-ups of one digital clock display reading 21:28 (32-39), which would teach red 7-segment digits as a microwave cue. Also a rating-label close-up, empty cabinets, an unrelated chrome object.

dishwasher.note: Removed an EU energy-label graphic, a 'Don't be a Dishwasher - BUY ONE!' cartoon advert, detergent-dispenser, cutlery-basket, hinge and dial close-ups, an installation collage, commercial kitchen scenes.

electric_fan.note: Keyword 'fan' matched sports fans (35,36), 'fan art' (28, a Godzilla cartoon), hand fans (0,2,19,29), cathedral fan vaulting (10), a butterfly, a bird, statues, alleyways and wall vents. Kept 17 electric fans, including a disassembled fan (37) that is ideal scrap context.

electric_motor.note: Keyword 'motor' matched an Amtrak locomotive (5-7), old trams, an electric car, a motorcycle wheelie (13), a motorcyclist, CGI rotor renders and N/S textbook diagrams, nameplate close-ups. Kept 16 real motors, including exposed windings (34) and coil rewinding (37): ideal scrap context.

generator.note: 29 kept: portable and industrial generator sets, genset enclosures and trailers. Removed: technical drawings, posters, nameplate closeups, stationary engines (not generators), control cabinets, aerials/landscapes, people shots.

air_cooler.note: Removed 8 1950s car-window 'swamp coolers' (evaporative coolers, but nothing like an Indian desert or room cooler), vintage cars, a VW Beetle, patent drawings and text pages, a spec label, a mosque interior, tents. Several kept units are one brand in transit stations, grouped by similarity.

inverter.note: 25 kept after re-query: home inverter+battery setups, wall-mounted solar inverters (incl rows in solar installations where inverter is prominent). Removed: solar-panel landscapes, diagrams, internals, connectors/parts, people, batteries alone, generator.

treadmill.note: Removed astronauts on the ISS (1-4,25), an underwater hydrotherapy pool (15,16), VR omni-treadmill renders and diagrams (26-28), a line chart (6), a historic treadwheel, a painting, a stage show, a hand-drawn sketch, and 10 handle or console close-ups.

laptop_screen.note: Mostly genuine laptops; #5 (streaked, damaged LCD) is ideal scrap context. Removed a cat filling the frame, circuit internals, person-focused portraits, cartoon and line-art illustrations, video-call screenshots, a game screenshot, a monitor showing an error screen.

desktop_cpu.note: Keyword 'tower' matched 17 buildings: the Eiffel Tower, Golden Gate Bridge, castles, cathedrals, skyscrapers, an airport control tower, Brasilia's congress towers. Also a sunset, a solid red frame, a labelled case diagram, a monitor. Kept 14 towers; 34 and 35 (grimy, rusted cases) are ideal scrap context.

crt_monitor.note: Strong class with ideal e-waste examples: smashed monitors with exposed boards (22,23,25,26) and one dumped in water (24). Removed electron-gun, anode and deflection-coil textbook diagrams (1,7,8,18,32), phosphor pixel macros, bare laboratory vacuum tubes, a label close-up.

lcd_led_monitor.note: 19 kept: flat-panel monitors front/back/on-desk, incl Apple displays. Removed: pixel macros, bare LCD modules/components, LED matrix panels, diagrams, laptops, scenes, scanner.

crt_television.note: Strong; includes a TV dumped on a street (30). Vintage TVs in museum displays are kept: collectors genuinely handle old CRT TVs, unlike archaeological artefacts. Removed the electron-gun diagram also filed under crt_monitor (0), Casio pocket LCD TVs that are not CRT at all (7-9), test-pattern close-ups, internals, a classroom, a street festival, a vintage radio.

printer.note: 39 kept: inkjets, lasers, MFPs, large-format. Removed: cartridges/parts alone, 3D printer, Game Boy printer, teletype, kiosks, diagrams, labels.

ups.note: 12 kept: UPS units (APC towers, MGE cabinet, rackmount, Back-UPS). Removed: schematics/block diagrams, bare PCBs/transformers/capacitors (e-waste parts, not UPS), motherboards, packaging boxes, people, server-room scenes, waveform, lighthouse.

smartphone.note: Good. Removed black abstract edge and screen shots with no recognisable phone, person-focused scenes (people at a railing, a hammock), a store advert poster, a ceiling interior, a speaker.

basic_mobile_phone.note: Search 'feature phone' matched Wikimedia's Featured Pictures, pulling in galaxies (32,33), a hot-air balloon, a red tractor, roller skates, a landscape painting, snowy mountains, birds at sunset, a collapsed house, a carpet, a Galileo plaque. Also lemons (27,28), likely via the Lemon phone brand, and two smartphones. Kept 12 keypad and flip phones.

tablet.note: 19 kept: tablet computers front/back/in-use, one disassembled (scrap-typical). Removed: graphics/drawing tablets (different device), phones, laptops, stylus accessories, people-focused, galaxy/star FP traps.

car.note: Good and on-target: scrapyards, crushed-car bales, rusted cars in fields. Removed a horse carriage, 'Tow Mater' from the Cars film at a theme park (38,39), a wing-mirror reflection, empty fields and skies, aerial landfill, and scrap-metal crane yards with no cars (4,5) that would contradict iron scrap.

scooter.note: 'Scooter' matched mobility scooters for the elderly (26-29), kick e-scooters (32,33), a Segway-like police vehicle (16-19), a utility cart, an e-scooter ban sign, fuel-gauge close-ups. Kept motor scooters only (the Indian sense, e.g. Activa); 9 is a burnt-out frame, ideal scrap context.

motorcycle.note: Label conflict: 23-34 are 12 near-identical shots of one parking lot of SCOOTERS, removed (they would inflate the test score and teach scooter as motorcycle). Also removed an art car, an alloy wheel, a river boat, a mountain landscape, an exhaust close-up. Kept includes a family on one bike (11) and a wrecked frame in snow (13).

bicycle.note: Cleanest class. Removed a puddle reflection, a stair ramp, a parking sign, a crankset and a saddle close-up, a bike-rack sculpture, a silhouette sculpture, a car, and a race photo that also appears under motorcycle (23).

geyser.note: First-ever geyser data: 20 kept. Removed: documents/drawings/text pages (5,13,21,45-54,56), adverts, different objects (doors, pots, stoves, HVAC, buildings), people/landscape shots.
